SUBJECT:  FIRST AMENDMENT TO LEGAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  KANE, BALLMER & BERKMAN, LLP INCREASING CONTRACT
  MAXIMUM BY $150,000

ISSUE
Approve a First Amendment to Legal Services Agreement with Kane, Ballmer &
Berkman, LLP increasing contract maximum by $150,000.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council/Successor Agency and Housing Authority:
  1. Approve a First Amendment to Legal Services Agreement with Kane, Ballmer &
  Berkman, LLP increasing contract maximum by $150,000.

BACKGROUND
The law firm of Kane, Ballmer & Berkman, LLP has represented the City for decades,
providing legal advice related to the dissolution of the former redevelopment agency,
housing law, development agreements, and related litigation. Kane, Ballmer & Berkman,
LLP currently provides general legal advice to staff and represents the Housing Authority
in the matter of Community Development Associates v. Housing Authority of the City of
Palmdale, et al. The present legal services agreement has a maximum contract amount
of $300,000.

DISCUSSION
To continue Kane, Ballmer & Berkman’s representation of the City, an amendment must
be executed to extend the contract maximum. By extending the contract maximum by
$150,000 we can continue to use the services of Kane, Ballmer & Berkman for our
ongoing litigation in Community Development Associates v. Housing Authority of the City
of Palmdale, et al., and for other legal services as stated above.
 Report to Mayor/Chair and City Council/Director/Commissioners
Re: Kane, Ballmer & Berkman, LLP
November 17, 2021
Page 2

FISCAL IMPACT
The Legal Services Agreement has the not-to-exceed amount of $300,000, however, this
amount is not guaranteed. This agreement will increase said amount by $150,000. Fees
will only be paid to the extent services are provided. Funds for this agreement are
currently budgeted in the City Attorney’s Office budget accounts, Litigation Account
(10114001-721140) - $391,051.00.

STRATEGIC PLAN
Goal II: Ensure long-term fiscal health of the City and maintain funding for services.
  A. Manage resources, costs and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.

SUBJECT:  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. CC 2021-107, A RESOLUTION OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE AUTHORIZING
  REMOTE TELECONFERENCE MEETINGS OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  AND ALL CITY SUBORDINATE BODIES FOR THE PERIOD OF
  NOVEMBER 20, 2021 – DECEMBER 20, 2021

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-107, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale Authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the City Council and All City
Subordinate Bodies for the Period of November 20, 2021 – December 20, 2021

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-107, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of Palmdale Authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the City Council
  and All City Subordinate Bodies for the Period of November 20, 2021 – December
  20, 2021

BACKGROUND
On September 16, 2021, the Governor signed AB 361 which temporarily amends the
Ralph M. Brown Act (California Government Code §§54950, et. al.) to provide more
flexibility regarding participation in public meetings from a remote location.

AB 361 went into effect October 1, 2021 and expires on January 1, 2024.

DISCUSSION
AB 361 requires several procedural safeguards to encourage maximum public
participation during a remote meeting, key ones of which are summarized as follows:
  1. The public must have the ability to address the legislative body directly and must
  be given information on how to address the legislative body;
  2. The public must be provided with either a call-in or internet-based service option;
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution No. CC 2021-107
November 17, 2021
Page 2

  3. The legislative body must stop the meeting if the call-in or internet-based option
  fails;
  4. The legislative body cannot require that public comments be submitted in
  advance (although this option can be provided);
  5. Public speakers cannot be required to pre-register for public comment (except as
  required by an independent call-in or internet platform);
  6. Members of the public must be given a reasonable time to register to provide
  public comment; and
  7. Agencies that provide a timed public comment period shall not close the public
  comment period until that time period has expired.
The proposed resolution would continue to permit meetings pursuant to AB 361 for a
maximum period of 30 days (November 20, 2021 – December 20, 2021).
Beyond this procedural requirement, there are no additional changes to the currently
established procedures regarding providing a teleconferencing option for public
meetings of the City Council and all of its subordinate bodies.
Accordingly, Staff recommends approval of Resolution No. CC 2021-107.
FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

STRATEGIC PLAN

   CITY COUNCIL
  CITY OF PALMDALE, CALIFORNIA
  RESOLUTION NO. CC 2021-107

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  AUTHORIZING REMOTE TELECONFERENCE MEETINGS OF THE
  CITY COUNCIL AND ALL CITY SUBORDINATE BODIES FOR THE
  PERIOD OF NOVEMBER 20, 2021 – DECEMBER 20, 2021

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale is committed to preserving and fostering public
access and participation in meetings of the City Council and all its subordinate bodies,
as required by the Ralph M. Brown Act (California Government Code §§54950, et. al.),
so that any member of the public may attend and participate as the bodies conduct the
public’s business; and

  WHEREAS, the Brown Act makes special provisions for remote
teleconferencing participation in meetings where the Governor has exercised his
authority pursuant to California Government Code § 8625, and an in-person meeting
may present imminent health risks to sitting members during public meetings; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Palmdale finds that the recitals found
to be true and correct in Resolution No. CC 2021-102 (passed on October 20, 2021),
incorporated herein by reference, continue to exist making remote participation in
meetings important to ensure the public is given full opportunity to participate; and

  WHEREAS, the City Council of the City of Palmdale finds that the City Council
and all of its subordinate bodies shall conduct their meetings with remote participation
in the manner authorized by California Government Code §54953(e), and such
legislative bodies shall comply with the requirements to provide the public with access
to the meetings as prescribed by California Government Code § 54953(e)(2).

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The Recitals set forth above are true and correct and are
incorporated herein by reference.

  SECTION 2. The City Council and its subordinate bodies shall conduct their
meetings with remote participation in a manner authorized by California Government
Code §54953(e), and such legislative bodies shall comply with the requirements to
provide the public with access to the meetings as prescribed by California Government
Code §54953(e)(2).
 Resolution No. CC 2021-107
Page 2 of 2

  SECTION 3. This Resolution shall take effect immediately upon its adoption and
shall be effective until the earlier of December 20, 2021, or such time as the City
Council adopts a subsequent resolution in accordance with California Government
Code §54953(e)(3) to extend the time during which meetings may continue to be held
remotely by teleconference in compliance with that section.

  SECTION 4. The City Clerk shall certify to the adoption of this resolution.

PASSED, APPROVED and ADOPTED this 17th day of November, 2021.

SUBJECT:  REVIEW AND APPROVE FY 2022 MEASURE AV BUDGET
  ADJUSTMENTS.

ISSUE
Review and approve FY 2022 Measure AV budget adjustments.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council review and approve the FY 2022 Measure AV
budget adjustments.

BACKGROUND
Each year, the City is required to adopt a balanced budget for the operations of the City.
The budget serves as the City’s financial plan for the fiscal year beginning July 1 through
June 30. It defines the City’s priorities for the provision of services to the community.

On May 18, 2021, the City Council was presented with a draft of the proposed Biennial
Budget for Fiscal Years 2021-23.

On May 19, 2021, the Measure AV Oversight Committee reviewed the proposed budget
and made a unanimous recommendation to the City Council to approve the proposed
Measure AV Fund budget.

On June 15, 2021, the City Council adopted the Biennial Budget for Fiscal Year 2021-
22 and Fiscal Year 2022-23.

On June 23, 2021, the Measure AV Oversight Committee was presented with the
Adopted Biennial Budget for Fiscal Year 2021-22 and Fiscal Year 2022-23 for Measure
AV and the City of Palmdale.

On August 25, 2021, the Measure AV Oversight Committee was presented with a
presentation on the City of Palmdale Grant Program, and potential use of Measure AV
funds for future grant programs.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: FY 2022 Measure AV Budget Adj.
November 17, 2021
Page 2

DISCUSSION
Measure AV went into effect April 1, 2021, and it was anticipated, at the time of budget,
that the City would generate approximately $15,500,000 in revenues in FY 2022 from
the ¾ cent sales measure. Sales tax is received from the State of California with
approximately a two-month lag. In FY 2021, from April through June, the City has
exceeded the projected revenues by approximately $2.2M. As a result, staff have
worked with the City’s sales tax consultant, HdL Companies, to perform analysis of sales
tax performance over the past quarter, and to revise the FY 2022 revenue projection.
Staff is proposing to increase both revenue and expenditures for Measure AV by
$1,500,000. The additional revenue would be used to support Grant Programs in the
City of Palmdale. The City of Palmdale Grant Program will allow the City to support local
businesses and non-profits, while providing much needed services to the community.
All grant funds to be awarded with Measure AV funds must be alignment with the
priorities of the ballot measure and will be subject to review by the Measure AV
Oversight Committee.

SUBJECT:  UPDATE ON AGREEMENT NO. A-7696 WITH DEARK E&C, INC.,
  FOR PROJECT NO. 813, PALMDALE FILM STAGES, LOCATED AT
  38448 SIERRA HIGHWAY

ISSUE
Update on Agreement No. A-7696 with Deark E&C, Inc., for Project No. 813, Palmdale
Film Stages, located at 38448 Sierra Highway.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Accept contractor’s resolution on Agreement No. A-7696 with Deark E&C, Inc.
  for the construction of Palmdale Film Stages located at 38448 Sierra Highway.

BACKGROUND
Capital Improvement Project No. 813 will refurbish the building at 38448 Sierra Highway,
Palmdale, CA 93550, to house the Palmdale Film Stages. The improvements include,
but are not limited to, building interior and exterior renovations, electrical upgrades, and
associated parking and accessibility improvements.

DISCUSSION
The City of Palmdale awarded Agreement No. A-7696 to Deark E&C, Inc. for Project No.
813, Palmdale Film Stages on November 4, 2021. At the time of award, Deark E&C,
Inc.’s electrical subcontractor was registered as a sole proprietorship with the California
State License Board and as a corporation with the Department of Industrial Relations.
This discrepancy was the source of a bid protest and per Council action, this discrepancy
was required to be resolved by November 17. On November 5, 2021, Deark E&C, Inc.
submitted the subcontractor’s Letter of Withdrawal, removing them from the Project.
Deark E&C, Inc. will have an electrician under their payroll to perform the work
themselves.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Update on Agreement No. 7696 Palmdale Film Stages
November 17, 2021
Page 2

The California Public Contract Code, Chapter 4 [4100-4114]/Section 4107 outlines
instances in which a prime contractor is allowed to substitute a subcontractor listed in the
original bid. Staff has determined that the criteria for substitution has been met, and Deark
E&C, Inc is allowed to self-perform in lieu of the electrical subcontractor.
